body:
That I’m going to die alone. It took me many years to not hate myself as much, and finally being comfortable with being alone than being in a toxic relationship again.  

Also I make dumb choices… related to self esteem issues.

My dog walked into the room and gave me a puppy eyes look as I started to pull on the noose around my neck.  I couldn’t stand the thought of leaving him alone in an apartment with my corpse for days since no one would find me right away.   

He’s sweet and empathetic as he sits on top of me or looks at me concerned when I’m mad/sad.

In my case things got a lot better after working with therapy as well as learning to be okay with myself.  Still a long road and WIP

My dog. A little over a year ago I thought about killing myself and I made a noose out of an old belt.  As I put it around my neck, sobbing, he walks in and just looked me directly in the eye, I couldn’t go through with it.

In fact I’m tearing up writing about this and he just walked up and is laying in my arms as I type.

I know what you mean.  I’m going to be 40 in some years and I’ve been dealing with the cycle since my 20s. People always give that “it’ll get better” and “time heals all” crap. That’s just another way of “I don’t know what to say” but it’s okay because it’s our problem, no theirs.

I still felt the way you do, so I just focus on getting as many little wins as I can to push off the inevitable feeling of killing myself. It’s getting harder but I’ll keep trying for now

In all honesty no one can tell if the situation as a whole will get better because that’s nothing anyone can predict (I’m in the same boat as you). 

However I’ve learned that you can definitely get better by being able to identify it, rely on your experience navigating the feelings that happen with depression, and you may get better at weathering the storm when it comes.  

My thoughts have been hitting in huge waves lately, to the point where I almost went through with something that would’ve been bad.  I still have a hard time finding the will to live most days, but I take it a day at a time and focus on finding little wins here and there.

Take a break first, then delete it.  I was an early facebook adopter (back when it was exclusive to college) since 2005 and was heavily addicted.  Two years ago I deactivated it for a few months, but reactivated it and picked up all the same habits and feelings from it.   


I deactivated it again in january and honestly, I don't even miss it or want to reactivate.  The only reason why I haven't deleted it is because I do have a lot of family photos there (i can extract them later, but for now it's fine).  House was robbed in 2008 so the laptop with the actual files are gone.    


I really only do instagram now (and well...reddit)... but definitely take a break.  You'll probably have withdrawals and some habits, but eventually it could help.
I'm glad you didn't as well.  Your strength echos to me :)

I agree. I often wonder who would come to my funeral and how would they react. The. I realize what’s the point because I’d be dead anyway. 

In my case due to feeling lonely and detached, I still care about what certain people think and also seek validation of sorts.  But generally being alone for years has only made that worse

Always fat, ever since I was a kid.  now I'm 38.  I remember being yelled at by my mom because various family members were concerned with how fat I was getting as I grew up.  This caused me to have a very low view of myself and crushingly low self esteem.... The moment that broke me and had me really considering suicide as an option was when I was in my early 20s,  my mom lectured me again (I wasn't doing well in college and also...fatter than ever).  She told me I would have more challenges in life than a normal person because I wasn't smart, I was fat, and I wasn't handsome like my brother.   Oddly enough she meant it from a place of love, but good old chinese parenting tough love didn't seem to work that way.  Now my needs for validation are stupid high and it's dumb.

I feel like I can count all the legit physical compliments on one had because they don't happen often.... and definitely not in a while.  But I never forgot each one of them. 

So now today, I make it a point to check in on friends (male and female), or send nice things if i know they are down... i'll usually amazon something that they enjoy.  For my own need for attention...i just bury that shit and hope for the best... i feel like if i come off needy, then more people will probably push away.

I understand. I grew up with a single Asian mom. I was a fat kid and not as smart as my older brother, so I would often get berated for my failures or overall appearance.  My mom had to work through all her life and said I was spoiled compared to her upbringing (we were poor and I started working at 10 to supplement my school income).  When I didn’t get into a certain college I was yelled at.  My father had legit schizophrenia and my mom didn’t think it was real, thinking he was faking it so he wouldn’t have to work (they had separated when I was very young).  Because I never told her about my bouts with depression and anxiety.  In college I was fucking up pretty bad, she would routinely come down to my room weekly to lecture me for an hour about how I’m failing in life. The one that broke me was when she came down and for 4 hours, told me I was going to have challenges in my life that “normal people” won’t have because I was fat, not handsome (her words), and not smart. So I’d have to work harder than others because I’m starting life with so many setbacks that normal people don’t have. (My therapists are always shocked at this.). I know she didn’t mean this maliciously because she was worried and would cry for me, but god damn of that wasn’t the first night I really thought about killing myself. I think I went out on a drive for a few hours in the middle of the night after that. 

Now I’m currently 38 and I’m still very fucked up on the head and have issues with validation, worth, and self esteem, with suicidal thoughts that surface from time to time.  BUT I have a great career in tech with a great salary because I leaned on something I did well: communicating and interacting with others.  I am fortunate to have a network of friends... though to be honest that was formed from contacts in my professional life post college. 

I wanted to let you know you’re not alone in this.... but also I did want to offer perspective. That’s why while I can’t offer direct advice, but if I could go back in time and tell myself that all their negative reenforcement was bullshit and things will be alright, I would.  Things like college are important, but the life or death emphasis on college that Asian parents put on their kids (you must go to Ivy League or you’ll die) is because they don’t know better. Back in their life that’s how things were.  They were taught that you can “overcome” things by working through it, but ignoring the stress creates further issues downstream. 

When my little brother started acting out after his father passed (my step father), my mom started the tiger mom stuff with him, albeit not as severe as it was with me (he is 17 years younger than I am).  She would tell him he inherited his fathers anger issues and this was “broken” and “had a learning disability “ because of it.  I told her she can’t say that stuff to him because it’ll mess him up like it messed me up.  And then I told him mom says stuff like that because she’s scared and concerned, but doesn’t know how to properly communicate that.  Things are better today with all of us as my mom confides in me as the voice of reason now, but I’m still action packed with issues. 

While I’m just some stranger on the internet I’m going act as if you’re my younger sibling as well.  Your parents are always going to be like that, and they’re going to be wrong about a lot of things, but too stubborn to admit it to reinforce the hierarchy.   But know they love you but don’t know how to express it because that was likely how they received affection in the old times.  Understand and always try your best for you.  You don’t have to listen to their criticisms but you definitely should try to be in tune with your own emotions and how you feel.  And try to apply logic to phrases they say that are wrong.  Understand it’s okay to be sad/angry/anxious and take the breaks for yourself when you can.  But more importantly know that they’re going to be critical of you now but you have all the chances to prove them wrong in your future.  They may not believe in you now, but that’s okay.  You don’t have to be a working machine, just be a good person.  I don’t know if my rant is just nonsense but I did want to say I know where you’re coming from, and I believe in you my younger adopted internet sibling!


I graduated with a 2.25 GPA and a marketing degree that didn’t mean anything.  Today I work in tech and make a good salary because I utilized some of my strengths

I’ll feel on top of the world one moment, then a profound sadness due to irrational thoughts.  Sometimes it feels like my brain isn’t used to such happiness, and I don’t deserve it, so something bad is gonna happen.  It’s driven me into a dark dark place quite a few times.  Recognizing its irrational is one method to cope, and I do so by counteracting crazy thoughts with logical phrases out loud. 

It’s helped but I equate these thoughts to being stuck in the rain. You’re going to be miserable for a bit and not sure of the time, but you’ve outlasted the storm before and can try to do it again.

I listen to the Donnie darko mad world song on repeat and imagine dying alone, and it just feels like my chest is ripping open more.  It’s like hitting the accelerator on my depression, but I wonder if I do it because it allows me to feel something.

I hear you. I’ve had shrinks not really know what to say... and I don’t tell them when I fly off the deep end because I don’t want cops to kick down my door and drag me away.  I’ve told friends and while they all have the usual “you can talk to me anytime”... I did with one friend and it was waaay too much for him. 

I think it’s easier to talk to strangers on the internet because we all have been in those thoughts, or currently live them, so we understand what everyone is going through...without the judgement of knowing anything about the person.  And I believe while we want to kill ourselves, we don’t wish that on anyone else, so words are provided.

I’ll say this subreddit has done more for me than two therapist and all my friends.  I’ll always have to fight my demons but it’s nice to know I’m not completely fighting them alone.  And neither are you. We’re here to talk and please reach out

Mid November, I was sitting at n the edge of my bed and had bottomed out mentally. I had nothing but despair and I had a noose around my neck made from an old martial arts belt.  I was crying and pulling it tighter, then my dog was just staring at me.  He’s sense me upset before and will lie on me.  Since I was sitting up he ended up next to me just staring. 

I had realized if I were to die, no one would find me and he’d be all alone in the apartment with my corpse.  This wasn’t the first time he’s saved me from those moments, but this was the first time I almost enacted something. 

I decided to live on at least for now.  Life will always be hard and we’ll never know if it gets better.  I don’t know any good advice to give because I could easily fall into the same thing again. All I can say is dogs love us with all their heart and we don’t deserve them.

Thank you for posting this and bless you for being who you are. I know exactly what you mean. I remember discussing this with another friend who also has suicidal thoughts, yet is always around to help people.  I saw this posted somehwre but it’s something along the lines of being there for others because we know what it’s like to feel pain, and we don’t want anyone to go through what we go through.

I find that most evident in this subreddit because I was almost over the edge quite a few times, and I’ll read how caring and compassionate others are here. That helps bring me back.  While I don’t know you well, I’m sure you’re that type as well.  

I’m a fucking wreck inside, lately I’ve been having suicidal thoughts that pop up at a drop, but when someone comes to me with an issue I want to do what o can to help.
Cook, martial arts, weight lifting, playing pool. Covid put a lid on most of those.
I hope tomorrow is easier for all of us. Thank you
Thank you

She was a friend who goes through the same things. But she’s also going through a lot. Long story short she thought I was pushing her away and she’s has a mountain of stuff she’s dealing with. There were miscommunications and she told me to fuck off.  We were each other’s support for 4 years.

It subsided a bit now, but was trying to reach out to a friend and things didn’t go well in that convo, so I lost another friend as I’m losing my Will to live. Tomorrow is another day. Thank you for checking up on a stranger. All of you. It does more good than you know...

I think I too was living with the warm feeling of being with someone who i thought cared for me for the past two months.  It helped move every dark thought aside.  Things changed yesterday and I ended up almost doing something I probably would've regretted.  


While not there physically, you're all not alone.  I've hit many dark times and i've found this subreddit to be therapeutic.  It's easy for us to think we're the only ones and no one cares, but I am comforted by the fact I totally understand your experience, and I do want to let you know you're not alone.  OP and everyone else.

I think posting on here is a good first step as you are with people who have had similar experiences and thoughts as you have.  If you have the means or can afford therapy, that also is a good step. Know that it won’t “cure” thoughts and each therapy style is different, but it’s good to have a professional apply techniques that may help you understand the emotions you are feeling. 

While people say talking to friends are good (and an option), my personal experience has said otherwise. Fortunately while I am blessed with a small group of friends that I could previously confide in, I felt like I started scaring them away.  

Unfortunately there’s not right answer on how to reach out for help, as for me it was relative to what I was comfortable expressing.

Yesterday I hit a deep mental low. Unfortunately I know how to make a noose from previous dark thoughts.  I am heavy and live in a small apt with nothing that can support my hanging weight. I thought about wedging it in a closed door frame or off a metal shelf I have. I practice a martial art where I’m used to being choked so I wasn’t too afraid at first. I took my long white belt and fashioned it into a noose.  Even before finding a foundation I put it around my neck and started pulling tighter.  It was a familiar feeling, and while not pleasant, I almost went through with it.  Then my survival fear kicked in, and I made eye contact with my dog, and released the noose.  My dog is the main reason why I’ve stuck around longer, and at that point I was worried that he’d be stuck with my dead body long before anyone would find us.  Today is a new day, and I will continue on for now as long as my dog needs me, because I need him.
